notes: BackOtter's KVM test hosts, one row each: the one table the test scripts take their host names, ssh targets, slot and port ranges, classes, roles and defaults from (testvm/test2/t2lib/hosts.py reads it; testvm/hosts.sh is the shell's reader; the scripts find it relative to themselves, here on the Mac and in ~/backotter-work/testvm on the hosts). Order matters: lists keep it, and the first fleet host holds vm-update's fleet lock. enabled false: a row reserved for a host that does not exist yet (its name and ranges are taken), which no script treats as a host. default true: a host of every run without --hosts (t2, drive.py); a host joins the defaults only after HostTest2 and one representative per family pass on it (docs/design/test2/design-classes.md); all four amd64 hosts of 2026-11-14 are default since then, copland and cage among them (the big hosts queued for hours while the small ones idled; what only a big host can run is kept there by each cell's ceiling and caps, never by a host's name); czerny joined the defaults 2026-11-19 by the user's choice; choubox joined the defaults 2026-11-17 by the user's choice, with its trial runs waived (the gate's bin cells, holt alpine324, artix-s6, debian13 and netbsd11 and stic mint22 and aerynos had passed there; its two HostTest2 loop cells can never fit its disk ceiling, 3.0 GiB of a 4G RAM disk). slot_range: the host's guest-slot range (guest-slot.sh's slot_range_here; run-all.sh's PORT_BASE is its first port, GUEST_PORTS the range); stic_ports: drive.py's check ports, inside it. ip: an address for when mDNS fails, with host_key_alias the name known_hosts pins it under (null: none known). A host's limits (limits: what each is, and its default) are its row's fields of those names, else class_limits' for its class, else the defaults, the values every host had before; the small class sets stic_slots 2, holt_jobs 1 and base_gib 4 (the user's choice, 2026-11-13); the big hosts keep the defaults but bs2_slots, 5 (small 2); chopin and cinqcent set holt_disk_mode true (the user's choice, 2026-11-14, for vanilla3's 30 GiB disk). RAM first, the SSD for overflow (the user's choice, 2026-11-23): both classes set scratch_mode overflow, so on the six test hosts a HoltTest line works in the RAM disk when its reservation fits there now, on /bkoscratch instead of waiting when it doesn't, and straight on /bkoscratch over ssd_cutoff_gib (12: truenas25's 27 GiB held chopin's whole RAM disk); with scratch off the RAM disk the memory is the limit, so holt_jobs went from 3 to 4 on the big hosts (4 GiB a job of a 25.2 GiB memory pool that SticTest and GuestTest share, 12 threads, and cinqcent held for swap-out that day) and from 1 to 2 on the M900s (12.1 GiB, 16 threads), choubox keeping its 1 (8.0 GiB, 4 threads); bigfoot's row keeps scratch_mode ram and holt_jobs 1, as it was. To put a host back: "scratch_mode": "ram" in its row (every host: in both classes), then sync. arch: the host's architecture, amd64 or arm64, amd64 when absent (every host before 2026-11-14): a guest runs only on a host of its own (a guest named *-arm64 is arm64, every other amd64; hosts.py guest_arch), and the x86-only loops (bs2, bko-holt shipping, build-round.sh's and promote-bins.sh's default hosts) take only amd64 hosts. job_slice: a systemd slice every heavy job on the host runs in (a guest's QEMU, cmp-run.sh's work), started by hosts.py job_prefix's sudo -n systemd-run --scope --quiet --slice=SLICE -- setpriv --reuid=USER --regid=USER --init-groups --reset-env -- CMD; vm-run and cmp-run.sh do it themselves; absent or null: none. rustup_home, cargo_home: absolute paths, or null (absent: none): the RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME the host's Rust builds take (hosts.py rust_env; build-round.sh, build-holt.sh and zig-tools.sh export them when unset), for a host whose pinned toolchains live apart from ~/.rustup and ~/.cargo. czerny: a MoreFine M900 like cage and copland (Ryzen 7 H 255, 16 threads, 27 GiB, a 10G RAM disk, host ZFS and bcachefs), enabled 2026-11-19 with cage's roles (build, cache), the small class's limits and its own range 3100-3199; default since 2026-11-19 (the user's choice). choubox: the user's GMKtec NucBox G3 Pro (i3-10110U, 4 threads, 15.5 GiB, 4G RAM disk, ARC capped at 512 MiB; joined 2026-11-17), small class with its own limits (1 stic slot, 1 holt job, 1 bs2 slot, base_gib 3: cmp-run.sh ceiling about 3.0 6.0; max_wall_x 2 since 2026-11-18, its slowness having cost flakes and reruns), cache role only, default since 2026-11-17; it is also the user's fallback bare-metal machine (BackShot-style runs when a distro rejects the Thinkpad), and such a run takes it out of the farm. bigfoot: the ARM64 host (docs/design/arm64.md), the user's daily machine, in bko.slice, its toolchains in /home/m/bko-arm64/toolchains; its one role is build-arm64 (A2: the round's native arm64 rustic-bko and arm64 bko-holt); it has no build, fleet, cache or store-mirror role, and it is also vm-store's master, which only Chopin (bigfoot-link) talks to, by its own name in vm-store (not this row).

classes.big: 62 GiB, a 30G RAM disk (cmp-run.sh ceiling about 23 GiB), host ZFS; build hosts
classes.small: guests from the image cache; copland, cage and czerny (M900s) 27 GiB, a 10G RAM disk, cmp-run.sh ceiling 9.0 10.1; choubox smaller, with its own limits (15.5 GiB, a 4G RAM disk, ceiling about 3.0 6.0)

roles.build: builds a round's binaries (stick/build-round.sh) and bko-holt
roles.build-arm64: builds a round's arm64 rustic-bko natively (stick/build-round.sh --arch arm64) and arm64 bko-holt (build-holt.sh linux-arm64); only an arm64 host has it, and it is not the build role
roles.fleet: holds every guest; vm-update keeps the fleet's copies alike
roles.bigfoot-link: the one host that talks to Bigfoot (vm-store push)

limits.stic_slots: SticTest's checks at once on the host (drive.py --slots); default 3
limits.guest_slots: guest slots drive.py counts on the host's range, 1-3 (check.sh's slot_take 3); default 3
limits.holt_jobs: HoltTest jobs at once on the host (ht1-queue.sh's MAXJOBS); default 3
limits.base_gib: cmp-run.sh's BASE_GIB on the host, GiB kept for the system (BASE_GIB in the environment wins); default 6
limits.holt_disk_mode: true: a holt line over the host's RAM-disk ceiling whose memory fits runs on /bkoscratch (HT_RAM=0, --reserve 0 M; NVMe wear), and placement checks its memory only (not +img: ht1.sh runs it only in the RAM disk); default false
limits.bs2_slots: BackShot2's tier 1 and 2 cases at once on the host (bs2-host queue --slots, each under cmp-run.sh --reserve 2 3), 1-6: the queue's ports are 2943-2948, 2949 a by-hand tier 1's; default 3. big 5: fits cmp-run.sh's memory check (5 x 3 GiB of about 23), unmeasured (2026-11-13); small 2, as bs2 had
limits.max_wall_x: t2's HoltTest2 and GuestTest2 cells a slow host leaves to the others (plan.Planner.fit_wall): a cell whose wall elsewhere (the median of its last 5 measured walls on the other hosts, PASS or FAIL, else its plan estimate) is over max_wall_x times its family's median wall elsewhere is kept off the host while another host of the cell's is left; a number 0.5 to 10, or null; default null (no cap). choubox 2 (the user's choice, 2026-11-18: no cell longer than about twice the median cell on the other hosts lands on the slowest host)
limits.scratch_mode: where a job that can work on either puts its scratch (HoltTest's lines; every other job's is in the RAM disk as ever): ram, in the RAM disk, waiting for its room there; overflow, in the RAM disk when its reservation fits there now, else on /bkoscratch instead of waiting (cmp-run.sh --reserve-ssd), and straight on /bkoscratch when it is over ssd_cutoff_gib; ssd, always on /bkoscratch. Never a +img line. A mode other than ram also does what holt_disk_mode does. The wear log says which it was (scratch=ram, scratch=ssd); default ram
limits.ssd_cutoff_gib: with scratch_mode overflow, a job whose scratch reservation is over this many GiB goes straight to the SSD; default 12
limits.ssd_floor_gib: the GiB of /bkoscratch that jobs' scratch never takes: a --reserve-ssd gets its room from the free space above it, less what the other SSD jobs hold, so a host short of free SSD gets no overflow; default 80
